source: 42 real auction threads from truedungeon.com, one per recorded auction, spanning 25 of the 33 forum auctioneers. Verbatim pages, gzipped, nothing trimmed — for the same reason fixtures/auction-open gives: the failures this guards against are matches found in the wrong place on the page, and a trimmed page cannot show one.
pagination: Kunena serves 12 posts to a page. Every page of every thread is here, because two of the assistant's outputs — the close-date evidence and the withheld candidates — live in later posts, not in the results post. `topic-N.html.gz` is page 1 and `topic-N-startM.html.gz` is the page beginning at post M.
sharedWithPhase4: Page 1 of 248428, 248693, 252093, 255503, 258020, 259475 and 259798 is NOT duplicated here — it already lives in fixtures/auction-open, which Phase 4 fetched from the same markup to read open dates. The test resolves page 1 from either directory. Copying them would leave two versions of one page in the repo, free to disagree after a re-fetch.

expect.why: The corpus totals, pinned so a regression reads as a number. `reproduces` is the quantity-weighted mode against prices.csv; `min` and `max` are what Trent's rule would have proposed from the same distributions, and the gap between them is the evidence that a thread wants a mode and a Trent file wants a pair. `closeBracketHits` is 12 of the 27 threads that yield a bracket at all, which is why the close date is reported as evidence and never proposed.

threads.why: TWO grammars in one post: a `Item | # | High Bidder | Current Bid` tab table for the premium items, and a headerless `qty | buyer | price` table for the trade goods beneath it. The header does not fit the second, so the reader falls back to reading it positionally — held to the first header those forty lines read as nothing at all. Also the plan's known disagreement: the thread says the Patron Pin went for $2.00 and the sheet records $1.25.

The results are a real HTML `<table>`, not tab-separated text — the only one in the corpus. Without a separator between cells the row arrives as `2019 Orb of Dragonkind1+$5.00$605maelios`. Also a thread whose post still says `Current Bids`, so its Patron Pin is $100.25 against a recorded $100.
The lot-RANGE grammar: `#1-3 : Lich - $100` is three tokens, not one. Reproduces every item it matches.
`1 $5.00 - Osiris` under an item heading ending in a colon — the count with no `x`, which means the price is each.

`Item (Qty) - $Price Buyer`, and `PYP 1 - $115.00 Moon` where the number is a lot number in the name. Carries the corpus's one true midpoint: Aragonite went 5 @ $16 and 5 @ $17 and is recorded as $16.50.

THE OFF-ORDER CASE and THE AMBIGUITY CASE. `NON-8K STUFF` heads twenty of his own tokens. They were discarded until 2026-08-24, on the reasoning that 20222 recorded none of them — but that was an unbackfilled season, not a decision, and the maintainer confirmed they are contextItems: the same names are already recorded as context for other auctions, including `Ioun Stone Gold Nugget`, `Charm of the Faerie`, `+4 Rod of the Meek` and eight `Folio` rows. The heading SCOPES, so they go to context whatever they resolve to; none of these twenty resolve in 2022, so the scoping is here for the next thread's, not for these. And nine lots are marked `ONYX or PYP`, which the sheet resolved BOTH ways: all nine are onyx.csv rows and their $110 is what prices.csv records as Ultra Rare. Also `x35 @ $12.25` — thirty-five bars at $12.25 each, the opposite of Flik's `10x $25`, and the `@` is the only thing that says so. The 21st Onyx row is the `Common, Uncommon, Rare Sets` line the sheet omitted in 2022 and has included since.

Matt Soto's grammar in another hand, with pseudonymous buyers (`16 @ $7.50 - Bidder #4`). Reproduces everything it matches — and its close-date bracket is 24 days early, the worst miss in the corpus and the reason that output is evidence rather than a proposal.

RESULTS IN POST #2, and NO DOLLAR SIGN ANYWHERE: `Orion's Belt (1) 150 Chronos`. A `$`-anchored parser reads this thread as empty. Its two Onyx rows — `Onyx Lucky Kilt` and `Onyx Death Knight Mail`, tokens he added from his own collection — are recorded NOWHERE: 202231 has no onyx.csv rows and no contextItems rows at all. Surfacing them is the assistant working, not failing, so the expected count here is what the thread says rather than what the sheet holds.
`Wish Ring (1) - $175.00 Abert` — the most common forum grammar there is, shared with Ralykam and with Wade S from 2025 on.

THE SECTION-END CASE. `ONYX ITEMS` is followed by `TRADE GOODS`, and without a rule that closes a section the Onyx heading runs to the bottom of the post: 33 Onyx rows proposed against 21 recorded, and eleven trade goods lost from the price spine. Its one tie, the Guild Button at 2 @ $1 against 2 @ $1.25, is recorded HIGH.
The plan's own worked example for the close-date bracket, and it lands: Feb 23-27 against a recorded Feb 25.
NO RESULTS ANYWHERE IN THE THREAD. The auction closed and shipped and the numbers were never posted. One of two threads that must produce nothing without pretending otherwise.

RESULTS IN POST #2, buyer-first (`- Anton (1) $780`), and the lot size written into the BUYER field: `- 10x Chips = Calnasse (4) $33` is four lots of ten at $3.30 a token. Also the `Avron's` typo: he drops a syllable from `Averon's Cherry Ale`, and until the resolver folded it the auction's 32 Preorder Bonus tokens were proposed as an augment named after the misspelling.

THREE MISSPELLINGS AND A BUNDLE, in an auction with only eight distinct names because a Safehold Onyx order keeps its content in onyx.csv. `Ring of the 3th Circle` is the whole 1k Bonus row (8 lots) and `3rd Mark of the Tenet (UR)` the whole 2k Bonus row (4 lots, $415) — an ordinal typo and an ordinal that migrated to the front of the name. `Charm of Brooching (1) - .$140 - Jo` carries a stray dot before the dollar sign. And its Safehold lot lists four parenthesised counts, the last of which a grammar took for the quantity: $1,555 proposed as $7,775.

ONE POST, BOTH MEANINGS OF `Nx`, and he says so: `Trade Goods (bidding on 10x lots or the specific amount)`. Above it `4x $130` is four Rings of the 3rd Circle at $130 each; below it `10x $35` is ten Minotaur Hides for $35. Read with one convention throughout, four prices come out wrong by their own lot size. Minotaur Hide is the tie that floating point decided — 36/35 and 3.6/3.5 are the same number and not the same double. Also `Mark of the Third Tenet`, the season's 2k Bonus with its ordinal spelled out.

NO SEPARATOR AT ALL between item and buyer — `Ring of the 3rd Circle Haliax $101` — so the split comes from the token index (threadBareLot) and, for a name no season knows, from the post's own set of buyers (threadBuyerLot). His trade-good headings declare their abbreviation, `Alchemist Ink (AI)` over eight lines of `AI X10 Wilem $21`. It read 1 of 19 before: `buyer-bare-price` had taken `Wish Ring Manet $146` for a bare buyer under a `PYPs (34)` heading and proposed an Ultra Rare at $146 against the recorded $80.
`(3) Lanfear====@ $105 each`. Two of its three misses are ties that resolved high.
The second thread with no posted results — the bids lived in a Google Sheet linked from post #1.
`10x 2025 Treasure Chips (5) - $35.00 Oghma` — the lot size in the NAME rather than on the line, which is `parseQuantity`'s rule and is shared with Trent unchanged.
The same auctioneer as 20181 seven years later, writing a completely different grammar. Whatever a parser learns from an auctioneer's old thread, it cannot assume about the new one.
PRICE LAST, BUYER IN THE MIDDLE: `Mark of the 1st Tenet (1) - Gortash $85`. Identical in shape to Beertram's line and reversed in meaning, so rule order is what tells them apart.

THE `Buy It Out` TRAP. The table is headed `item name | Buy It Out | Bid | Bidder/Buyer Name`: the money-formatted column is a buy-it-now price, identical down every row of an item, and the winning bid is the bare column beside it. Reading the formatting scores 6; reading the header scores 14. Its unresolved lines are exactly the five grunnel and augment rows contextItems carries for this auction.

threads.onyxNote: 21, not the 20 measured before the item-price-dash-buyer grammar existed. `Onyx Greaves of Diffusion - $65 - Allen` puts a DASH before the buyer where the rest of this post puts a space, so it was the one Onyx line no grammar read. onyx.csv records 21 rows for this auction, so 21 is the reconciling number and the old 20 was encoding the miss.
threads.why: The plan's withheld example, verbatim: "For this auction I am keeping the 9-10 random URs, 2 OE and 2 EB out." Quantities as a RANGE, which is why withheld candidates are quoted for a human rather than parsed into a row.

THE `Nx` CASE, both ways in one post. Under `Alchemist's Ink (33)`, `10x $25` is ten tokens for $25 — $2.50 each. Under `Aragonite (12 - individual)`, `9x $11` is nine tokens at $11 each. Only the heading's `individual` tells them apart, and getting it wrong is a factor of ten either way. Also `+2 Branding Mace // $42 - Samantha` under an `Onyx URs (16)` heading, where the heading is the ONLY thing marking sixteen chase tokens as Onyx — and `Standard Onyx 8k Items`, a heading that must NOT be read as one.

The file path's auctioneer. He posts no per-item results at all — the thread links a tracking spreadsheet — which is exactly why part one exists. Present so the two halves of Phase 5 are visibly complementary rather than overlapping.

threads.withheldQuote: only keeping the eight Rings of the First Circle
threads.why: THE REPOSTED-SNAPSHOT CASE, and the reason post #1 wins. He reposts the whole table as a bid update: 80 of its 165 posts carry a near-complete copy and the BIGGEST copy is a mid-auction snapshot whose prices are lower. "The post with the most lots" picks that one and reproduces nothing; post #1, edited in place after the close, reproduces all fifteen. Its withheld sentence appears 71 times and is 4 distinct sentences, which is why candidates are deduped — and the right one, `Ring of the 1st Circle` × 8, is exactly what contextItems records. Also `Tabor's onyx dagger #3`, a physical prop that must NOT be routed to onyx.csv just for containing the word.
The auction part one imports from a file. No per-item results in the thread, but its close-date bracket lands exactly on the recorded date — the plan's second worked example.

THE CONDENSED-BAG CASE. A Condensed order sells a bag of 120 random Rares and a bag of 240 random Uncommons, which no Super or Ultra Condensed auction has. This auctioneer writes them `8 x 120 Random Rare bag`, and that leading `8 x ` is read by the shared quantity rule as a lot of 8 — so the $100 bag divides to $12.50 unless a bag is exempted. Its two recorded bag prices are reproduced exactly, which is what pins both halves of the fix. itemsMatched is 0 because this auctioneer's other line grammars are not supported; the bags are what this fixture is here for.

A Condensed auction MISSING its bag rows — one of three found by the new check. Its `TOKEN BAGS` section sells `Bag of 120x Rare Tokens` and `Bag of 240x Uncommon Tokens`, and the Rare Bag is a genuine 4-4 tie ($70 and $65), so it exercises the tie flag on a proposal for data the sheet does not yet hold.

The quantity as a PREFIX rather than a parenthetical, with the dash before the buyer optional: `20 Alchemist's Parchment - Flind $2` and `20 Alchemist Ink Kobold $7.25` are the same lot shape. The bare form cannot say where the item ends and the buyer begins, so it defers to the heading. Also the two headings that quote a floor — `PYP's (68) (Minimum bid $50)` — which threadLooksLikeHeader has to let through on the strength of the parenthetical being a minimum, or the Ultra Rares land under `Orbs of Dragonkind`. Two items still read short: the orb variant is spelled `Great Wrym` and the four prior-season URs at the top are genuine augments.

Casey Wren WITHOUT his leading dash. `Zani (1) $376` under an `Orb of Dragonkind [Great Wyrm] (1)` heading is the same shape as 20242's `- Anton (1) $780`, and requiring the dash read this auction as nothing at all.

A price with NO dollar sign: `Ring of the 5th Circle (2) - Hank @ 75`. Utterly consistent otherwise, and the missing `$` alone read the auction as 0 of 23. The premium items drop the parenthetical — `Wish Ring - Hand Witch @ 185` — which is why there are two rules. He also calls a Treasure Chip a Treasure Token and writes the three out: `3x Treasure Tokens (16) - Reginald @ 7.25` is sixteen lots of three at $2.42. The four unresolved lines are the Mage Medallion order and its augments.

The same shape as 20226 but TAB-separated, which sends it down the positional table reader instead of the line rules. `Calnasse | (5) | $91.00` has a name in the first cell, so read the plain way the BIDDER becomes the item and six trade goods are lost. A parenthesised count in its own cell is what marks it — the only thread in this corpus or the fifty 2022 threads that writes one.

The buyer is a NUMBER. `1 @$310 #007`, `2@40$  012` with the dollar sign after the price, `8@82 001` with none at all, `17  @$.25 #006` with no leading zero, and the `#` optional throughout — one shape under a clean header/detail post, wearing every inconsistency at once.

A THIRD Casey Wren format — `Anton $370.00` and `Selvra 5 @ $30.00`, quantity after the buyer — and the lot size stated in the HEADING as `Alchemist Parchment 10x Chip`. parseQuantity reads a lot size off the front of a name, so the suffix has to be moved there: five chips at $30 is fifty tokens at $3.00, which is what prices.csv records. Left alone the heading resolves to nothing and twenty-one trade-good lines are proposed as augments.

A TAB-SEPARATED table with no header row: `1 | Wish Ring | @ | $190.00 | - | Garfield`. It read 0 of 21 because the positional reader treats a bare first cell as a quantity and the NEXT cell as the buyer — Wade S's `10 | Echo | $3.25` shape — so the item name went into the buyer field and `8k Exclusives:` became the item for four lots. Then `Onyx:` cleared the heading and the remaining 56 lines were dropped as "no item name above it". What separates the two tables is whether anything follows the price. Also `Pick Your Purple URs`, which is PYP written out, and `Common UC Rare Set` for `C/UC/R Set`.

The same table as 202336 with two AUGMENT sections, which is what makes it worth keeping separately: `Super Special Relics:` and `Augmented Ultra Rares:` scope to contextItems, and neither closed the `Onyx:` section before — so nine of Kusig's own tokens were proposed as Onyx rows, 28 against the 21 recorded, and four of the 21 came out at the augment's price because both lots resolve to one name (`+2 Sun Scimitar` $51 against a recorded $67). It also pins that an off-order heading OUTRANKS an `(Onyx)` marker: without that the same section splits down the middle on a suffix. The three unreproduced prices are mode-vs-sheet disagreements, not parse failures — a genuine 2-vs-2 tie on the Pointy Stick, and two where the sheet takes the lower of two quantity-weighted prices.

ALL-CAPS BIDDER NAMES. `10 @ $3.00 - THE PRESENCE` and `3 @ $95 FIDDLER'S GREEN` reduce to multi-word all-caps strings, so threadSectionOf read each as a heading that CLOSED the open section — taking the item heading with it, so the line below had no name either. 3 of 23. Also `(xN)` in a heading, which is the stock available and not part of the name, and a PYP block that drops the dash before the buyer. THIS THREAD WAS ALSO A DATA FINDING: 13 of its 23 prices disagreed with prices.csv, and the parser was right about all of them — the sheet was stale and the maintainer republished it to match (PR #102). It had looked like Tyler's table listing winning BIDS where the sheet recorded what was PAID, which his own rules make plausible. It was not. All 23 now reproduce, which is what this fixture pins.

Lord Brian's `(N)Buyer====@price` written three looser ways, each of which costs a whole item because Steve gives an item one or two lines: no `@` at all (`(8) Hermione==========.25`), no leading zero on the price, no closing paren (`(10Moody=========@12.00`), and no parenthetical at all on a one-of-one lot (`Dumbledore========@575.00`, which is the 8k Bonus). He writes no `$` anywhere, which is also why the header guard had to stop looking for one. Carries the malformed-money case: `(28)Harry======@3..75` is 28 of 48 Minotaur Hides and truncated to $3.00 against a recorded $3.75 — refused now, and the item's other line prices it correctly.

A FOURTH Casey Wren format: `Item` heading, then `- Buyer (qty) $price`. The one-of-one lots drop the parenthetical — twelve lines of `- Zani $105` — and every one of them is an item in its own right, including `Patron Pin` and `Patron Token 1` (the 2023 Charm of Biting). Also one line where he forgot the `$`: `- Vestia (38) 5.50`. Reproduces all 19 recorded prices.

THE OTHER READING OF `Nx`, and the reason 20264 has to stay in this corpus beside it. Flik writes `10x $25` in 2026 meaning ten tokens for $25, and `21x $4.00` here meaning twenty-one at $4 each — same shape, opposite meaning, same auctioneer. Read as a lot the way 20264's is, EVERY trade good in this thread was divided twice (the heading's lot size on top): Alchemist's Ink $0.19 against a recorded $4.25, Ultra Rare $5.94 against $95, 3 of 21 prices right. The parse rated 21 of 22 items matched throughout, because `matched` compares names. Settled by which reading makes the unit prices agree, with the decidable groups in a post voting for the ones whose lines all carry the same count. Also `2023 3x Treasure Chips`: this season's own year in front of a name hides the lot size from parseQuantity, and the chips came out at $8.75 against a recorded $2.92, which is $8.75 / 3.

Lord Brian writes his augments with his two separators BOTH ways round — `Item - Buyer = $price` five times and `Item = Buyer - $price` three times — and only the first had a rule. The other three were read by item-buyer-dash-price, whose name group is lazy, so it split on the first dash it found and `2020 UR Semi-Lich Skull = Nynaeve - $60` became an item called `2020 UR Semi`. A proposal under half a word is worse than none. Pins three things at once: the new rule, that a hyphen inside a word is not a separator, and that the YEAR in front of a `UR` marker comes off with it — the two line shapes disagreed about that, so one post proposed `Mad Evoker's Charm` and `2021 UR Mad Evoker's Charm` as two different context items. All eight of the auction's recorded contextItems rows are now reproduced by name and price.
